answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it earns influence, then weight decisions by bond rather than by account count. A newcomer may create a thousand identities, but splitting one deposit among them does not create more voting power; funding each separately raises the attacker’s capital at risk. If linked accounts coordinate a provable exploit, the protocol can seize their bonds. A basalt ledger may record commitments, while a river of transactions reveals patterns; a sparrow-sized stake still buys little sway.
